claude.sample_unit: structured observations of nurses' practices (9 ICU nurses; 165 patients tracked for incidence; 7 nurses interviewed)
models_evaluated: CDSS-PIRM (Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management)

links.outcome: Pressure injury incidence across pre-test and two post-implementation stages
links.effect: Incidence unchanged: overall 10.9%; pre-test 9.68%, post-test 1 11.63%, post-test 2 11.67%; p = 0.920, despite improved practice scores
links.quote: Overall pressure injury incidence remained unchanged (10.9%; pre-test: 9.68%; post-test 1: 11.63%; post-test 2: 11.67%; p = 0.920).

links.outcome: Nurses' experiences of workflow integration of the CDSS
links.effect: Nurses reported benefits but also barriers to clinical integration: workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue, and infrastructure limitations
links.quote: Two main themes were identified: (i) experienced benefits (a comprehensive clinical guide with real-time prevention support and advanced documentation); and (ii) barriers to clinical integration (workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations).

openai.sample_unit: structured observations of ICU nurses' pressure injury risk management practices
models_evaluated: Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management (CDSS-PIRM)

links.outcome: Wound care practice scores during implementation with real-time alerts
links.effect: At post-test 2, with real-time alerts, wound care scores improved: median 1.5 [IQR 0-2] vs. 0 [IQR 0-1]; p = 0.015.
links.quote: Risk assessment practice scores were significantly higher at post-test 1 compared with the pre-test (median 3 [IQR 2-6] vs. 2 [IQR 1-2]; p = 0.016), while wound care practice scores improved significantly at post-test 2 (median 1.5 [IQR 0-2] vs. 0 [IQR 0-1]; p = 0.015).

links.outcome: Pressure injury incidence across implementation stages
links.effect: Pressure injury incidence remained unchanged: overall 10.9%; pre-test 9.68%; post-test 1 11.63%; post-test 2 11.67%; p = 0.920.
links.quote: Overall pressure injury incidence remained unchanged (10.9%; pre-test: 9.68%; post-test 1: 11.63%; post-test 2: 11.67%; p = 0.920).

links.outcome: Nurse-reported barriers to clinical workflow integration
links.effect: Interviews with seven nurses identified workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations as integration barriers.
links.quote: Two main themes were identified: (i) experienced benefits (a comprehensive clinical guide with real-time prevention support and advanced documentation); and (ii) barriers to clinical integration (workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations).

screen.practice: real-time alerts vs passive decision support
screen.reason: The study evaluates a CDSS for pressure injury risk management deployed in an ICU, comparing implementation without real-time alerts versus with real-time alerts across stages.
